"Our country needs unity, peace and a president of whom all Hungarians can be proud," Peter Magyar said in a Facebook post, adding that he will meet with Polgar on Tuesday to ask her if she would be willing. Hungarian lawmakers last week passed an amendment that will remove current President Tamas Sulyok, an ally of former prime minister Viktor Orban.

Analysts noted Kazakhstan fits the profile of the simulated adversary as over 47,000 troops conducted maneuvers integrating tactical lessons from the war in Ukraine. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 3, 2026, 10:22 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Russian President Vladimir Putin (C) visits an observation post during the “Center-2026” strategic command-and-staff exercise at the Chebarkulsky training ground in Chelyabinsk Region on Oct. 2, 2026. (Photo by Alexander KAZAKOV / POOL / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Russian armed forces practiced transitioning from defensive operations to a counter-offensive and carving out a “security zone” inside the territory of a neighboring state during the large-scale strategic military exercise Tsentr-2026, according to official Kremlin dispatches and Russian defense ministry briefings. The maneuvers, conducted between Sept. 28 and Oct. 3, were formally designated to practice repelling conventional aggression on the Central Asian strategic vector and ensuring military security across the Caspian Sea basin. However, operational details presented to Russian President Vladimir Putin revealed that the drills incorporated cross-border offensive actions. Reporting to Putin on the progress of the maneuvers, Russian Deputy Defense Minister Yunus-Bek Yevkurov stated that after repelling an adversary’s opening assault, coalition forces launched a large-scale counter-offensive. Advertisement Yevkurov detailed that starting Oct. 2, troops rehearsed operations to “liberate seized territory” and establish a “security zone on adjacent territory” belonging to the opposing state. Putin traveled in person to the Chebarkul military training ground in the Chelyabinsk region on Friday, Oct. 2, to observe the concluding phase of the exercises, stating that Russian formations were directly integrating operational tactics and doctrine developed during the full-scale war in Ukraine. Central Asian vector While Russian defense officials did not formally name the hypothetical neighboring adversary, defense analysts at Ukrainian military portal Militarnyi noted that Kazakhstan most closely matches the operational geography of the scenario. Kazakhstan shares an extensive land border with Russia’s Chelyabinsk region where the Chebarkul training facility is situated, represents a central political entity in Central Asia, and possesses an extensive coastline along the Caspian Sea. Analysts emphasized that while the operational design closely mirrors regional geography, the identification of Kazakhstan remains an analytical assessment rather than an officially confirmed element of Moscow’s war games. Advertisement The strategic maneuvers involved significant firepower across multiple domains. Four Russian long-range strategic bombers conducted simulated strikes against designated “critical infrastructure” of the adversary, supported by tactical aviation, artillery units, strike drones, mechanized armored columns, and surface combatants of the Caspian Flotilla. According to Russian defense ministry figures, the Tsentr-2026 exercise mobilized more than 47,000 military personnel, over 2,000 pieces of heavy weaponry and military hardware, 90 combat and transport aircraft, and 77 naval ships and support vessels. Operations were executed across 11 designated military ranges and the maritime zone of the Caspian Sea. Moscow additionally hosted foreign military contingents from Belarus , China , Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Pakistan, and Tajikistan. European pre-war legislation The offensive maneuvers in Central Asia coincide with heightened defense vigilance across NATO’s eastern flank, where frontline European governments are preparing for prospective cross-border escalation. Advertisement In Poland , the Ministry of National Defense confirmed on Friday that it is drafting comprehensive legislation to introduce a formal “pre-war” phase of defense readiness , enabling early troop deployments and institutional mobilization before martial law is legally declared. The draft statute is designed to bridge the regulatory gap between peacetime governance and wartime mobilization, linking national operational plans directly to NATO’s Response System. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has repeatedly warned that Europe has entered a “pre-war era,” cautioning that allied intelligence dispatches indicate Moscow is evaluating hybrid drone and missile strikes against nations supporting Kyiv , which the Kremlin could portray as accidents to test the resolve of NATO’s Article 5 collective defense guarantee. The legislative drive also follows escalatory rhetoric from senior Russian officials directed at frontline European states. Former Russian President Dmitry Medvedev threatened Lithuania in September with destruction if it rescinded restrictions on nuclear weapons, asserting NATO would not risk global war to defend Vilnius. Days later, Kremlin security aide Nikolai Patrushev threatened that Moscow could deploy its “entire arsenal” against Poland , claiming Warsaw could be destroyed within days following Polish warnings that the alliance would decisively defeat any conventional Russian attack.
